views.name: orders_enriched_with_store_channel_hub
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  orders.order_id AS order_id,
  orders.store_id AS store_id,
  orders.channel_id AS channel_id,
  orders.payment_order_id AS payment_order_id,
  orders.delivery_order_id AS delivery_order_id,
  orders.order_status AS order_status,
  orders.order_amount AS order_amount,
  orders.order_delivery_fee AS order_delivery_fee,
  orders.order_delivery_cost AS order_delivery_cost,
  orders.order_created_hour AS order_created_hour,
  orders.order_created_minute AS order_created_minute,
  orders.order_created_day AS order_created_day,
  orders.order_created_month AS order_created_month,
  orders.order_created_year AS order_created_year,
  orders.order_moment_created AS order_moment_created,
  orders.order_moment_accepted AS order_moment_accepted,
  orders.order_moment_ready AS order_moment_ready,
  orders.order_moment_collected AS order_moment_collected,
  orders.order_moment_in_expedition AS order_moment_in_expedition,
  orders.order_moment_delivering AS order_moment_delivering,
  orders.order_moment_delivered AS order_moment_delivered,
  orders.order_moment_finished AS order_moment_finished,
  orders.order_metric_collected_time AS order_metric_collected_time,
  orders.order_metric_paused_time AS order_metric_paused_time,
  orders.order_metric_production_time AS order_metric_production_time,
  orders.order_metric_walking_time AS order_metric_walking_time,
  orders.order_metric_expediton_speed_time AS order_metric_expediton_speed_time,
  orders.order_metric_transit_time AS order_metric_transit_time,
  orders.order_metric_cycle_time AS order_metric_cycle_time,
  stores.store_name AS store_name,
  stores.store_segment AS store_segment,
  stores.store_plan_price AS store_plan_price,
  stores.store_latitude AS store_latitude,
  stores.store_longitude AS store_longitude,
  hubs.hub_id AS hub_id,
  hubs.hub_name AS hub_name,
  hubs.hub_city AS hub_city,
  hubs.hub_state AS hub_state,
  hubs.hub_latitude AS hub_latitude,
  hubs.hub_longitude AS hub_longitude,
  channels.channel_name AS channel_name,
  channels.channel_type AS channel_type
FROM orders
LEFT JOIN stores ON orders.store_id = stores.store_id
LEFT JOIN hubs ON stores.hub_id = hubs.hub_id
LEFT JOIN channels ON orders.channel_id = channels.channel_id

params.description: A per-order enriched view that returns one row per order with order attributes, timestamps, computed order-level timing metrics, and joined store, hub and channel descriptive fields.
params.when_to_use: Report or dashboard that needs order-level detail (amounts, fees, status) together with store, hub and channel metadata. | Build aggregations by summing or averaging order_amount, delivery fees or timing metrics grouped by time, store, hub or channel. | Join to other one-row-per-order facts (payments_by_order_agg, deliveries_by_order_agg) to add payment/delivery aggregates by order without additional grouping. | Drill-down from aggregated summaries (e.g., orders_daily_counts_and_amounts) to the underlying order rows for debugging or row-level exploration.
params.output_schema: order_id: unique identifier of the order; derived from orders.order_id | store_id: store identifier that received the order; derived from orders.store_id | channel_id: channel identifier that created the order; derived from orders.channel_id | payment_order_id: payment reference for the order; derived from orders.payment_order_id | delivery_order_id: delivery reference for the order; derived from orders.delivery_order_id | order_status: current status of the order (string/enum); derived from orders.order_status | order_amount: monetary amount charged for the order; derived from orders.order_amount | order_delivery_fee: fee charged to customer for delivery; derived from orders.order_delivery_fee | order_delivery_cost: cost incurred for delivery; derived from orders.order_delivery_cost | order_created_hour: integer hour component of order creation time; derived from orders.order_created_hour | order_created_minute: integer minute component of order creation time; derived from orders.order_created_minute | order_created_day: integer day of month of order creation; derived from orders.order_created_day | order_created_month: integer month of order creation; derived from orders.order_created_month | order_created_year: integer year of order creation; derived from orders.order_created_year | order_moment_created: timestamp when order was created; derived from orders.order_moment_created | order_moment_accepted: timestamp when order was accepted by store; derived from orders.order_moment_accepted | order_moment_ready: timestamp when order was marked ready; derived from orders.order_moment_ready | order_moment_collected: timestamp when order was collected by driver; derived from orders.order_moment_collected | order_moment_in_expedition: timestamp when order entered expedition/hub flow; derived from orders.order_moment_in_expedition | order_moment_delivering: timestamp when delivery started towards customer; derived from orders.order_moment_delivering | order_moment_delivered: timestamp when delivery reached customer; derived from orders.order_moment_delivered | order_moment_finished: timestamp when order was finished/closed; derived from orders.order_moment_finished | order_metric_collected_time: numeric metric (seconds/minutes) representing time spent at collection stage; derived from orders.order_metric_collected_time | order_metric_paused_time: numeric metric representing paused time in the order lifecycle; derived from orders.order_metric_paused_time | order_metric_production_time: numeric metric representing time spent in production/preparation; derived from orders.order_metric_production_time | order_metric_walking_time: numeric metric representing walking time (likely driver) portion of order; derived from orders.order_metric_walking_time | order_metric_expediton_speed_time: numeric metric representing expedition/hub processing speed/time; derived from orders.order_metric_expediton_speed_time | order_metric_transit_time: numeric metric representing transit time to customer; derived from orders.order_metric_transit_time | order_metric_cycle_time: numeric metric representing total cycle time for the order; derived from orders.order_metric_cycle_time | store_name: human-friendly store name; derived from store.name (joined) | store_segment: categorical segment of the store (e.g., vertical); derived from store.segment (joined) | store_plan_price: numeric store plan/price tier; derived from store.plan_price (joined) | store_latitude: store latitude coordinate; derived from store.latitude (joined) | store_longitude: store longitude coordinate; derived from store.longitude (joined) | hub_id: hub identifier associated with the order (nullable); derived from hub.hub_id (joined) | hub_name: hub human-friendly name; derived from hub.name (joined) | hub_city: hub city; derived from hub.city (joined) | hub_state: hub state/region; derived from hub.state (joined) | hub_latitude: hub latitude coordinate; derived from hub.latitude (joined) | hub_longitude: hub longitude coordinate; derived from hub.longitude (joined) | channel_name: human-friendly channel name; derived from channel.name (joined) | channel_type: channel type/category; derived from channel.type (joined)
params.grounded_columns: orders.order_id | orders.store_id | orders.channel_id | orders.payment_order_id | orders.delivery_order_id | orders.order_status | orders.order_amount | orders.order_delivery_fee | orders.order_delivery_cost | orders.order_created_hour | orders.order_created_minute | orders.order_created_day | orders.order_created_month | orders.order_created_year | orders.order_moment_created | orders.order_moment_accepted | orders.order_moment_ready | orders.order_moment_collected | orders.order_moment_in_expedition | orders.order_moment_delivering | orders.order_moment_delivered | orders.order_moment_finished | orders.order_metric_collected_time | orders.order_metric_paused_time | orders.order_metric_production_time | orders.order_metric_walking_time | orders.order_metric_expediton_speed_time | orders.order_metric_transit_time | orders.order_metric_cycle_time | store.store_id | store.name | store.segment | store.plan_price | store.latitude | store.longitude | hub.hub_id | hub.name | hub.city | hub.state | hub.latitude | hub.longitude | channel.channel_id | channel.name | channel.type
params.metric: order_amount = orders.order_amount (base monetary field, additive across orders) | order_delivery_fee = orders.order_delivery_fee (base monetary field, additive across orders) | order_delivery_cost = orders.order_delivery_cost (base monetary field, additive across orders) | order_metric_collected_time = orders.order_metric_collected_time (order-level duration metric; can be averaged or summed across disjoint sets of orders) | order_metric_paused_time = orders.order_metric_paused_time (order-level duration metric) | order_metric_production_time = orders.order_metric_production_time (order-level duration metric) | order_metric_walking_time = orders.order_metric_walking_time (order-level duration metric) | order_metric_expediton_speed_time = orders.order_metric_expediton_speed_time (order-level duration metric) | order_metric_transit_time = orders.order_metric_transit_time (order-level duration metric) | order_metric_cycle_time = orders.order_metric_cycle_time (order-level duration metric)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to store dimension/view on orders.store_id = store.store_id — safe because store is one-row-per-store, so augmenting this view with store attributes will not duplicate order rows or its measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to channel dimension/view on orders.channel_id = channel.channel_id — safe because channel is one-row-per-channel, so measures remain one-per-order. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hub dimension/view on orders.hub_id = hub.hub_id (if hub_id exists in orders) — safe because hub is one-row-per-hub; the join preserves one row per order. | safe-to-join facts: join to payments_by_order_agg ON orders.order_id = payments_by_order_agg.order_id — safe because payments_by_order_agg is an aggregation pre-rolled to one row per order (AGG sibling). | safe-to-join facts: join to deliveries_by_order_agg ON orders.order_id = deliveries_by_order_agg.order_id — safe because deliveries_by_order_agg is aggregated to one row per order. | do NOT join directly to tables or views that are one-to-many relative to order (for example: order_items, promotions_per_order, driver_events where multiple events per order exist) without first aggregating them to one row per order. Doing a direct one-to-many join will multiply order rows and thus inflate additive metrics like order_amount or summed timing metrics. | when composing up (aggregating this view): sum(order_amount), avg(order_metric_cycle_time) and count(distinct order_id) are correct. If you need metrics that depend on multiplicity (e.g., items per order), derive them from a one-row-per-order source or pre-aggregate the many-side and then join. | if joining to drivers_with_delivery_stats (AGG) — ensure the join key is a one-to-one mapping (e.g., driver_id when drivers_with_delivery_stats is one-row-per-driver). If drivers_with_delivery_stats is one-row-per-driver and orders have many orders per driver, joining will create multiple rows per driver but preserve correct order-level measures because the driver side is one-row-per-driver (i.e., the order rows remain atomic). Do not join a driver-events raw table without aggregation.

views.description: Denormalized order-level relation joining orders to store, channel and hub descriptive attributes. Useful as a starting point for analytics that need store, channel, or hub context for each order (e.g., revenue by store, orders by channel, location-based reporting). Keeps one row per order_id and preserves the original order-level measures and timestamps. | Use for: Revenue, counts and averages by store, channel, hub, date parts; Order lifecycle timing and delivery performance by store or hub; Geo-based or segment-based order distributions

views.name: payments_by_order_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  payment_order_id AS payment_order_id,
  COUNT(payment_id) AS payments_count,
  SUM(payment_amount) AS payments_amount_sum,
  SUM(payment_fee) AS payments_fee_sum,
  MIN(payment_status) AS payment_status_any -- preserves a status value when needed; callers can inspect / filter
FROM payments
GROUP BY payment_order_id

params.description: Aggregated per-order payment metrics: count, total amount, total fee, plus a representative payment status.
params.when_to_use: Get payment-level summary metrics per order (how many payments, total paid amount, total fees). | Join payment aggregates into an order-level result set without duplicating payment measures. | Filter or route orders by a preserved example payment_status when a status value is needed for inspection or filtering. | Compose higher-level metrics (e.g., revenue per order, net amount) by building on these per-order aggregates.
params.output_schema: payment_order_id: the order identifier used to group payments — derived from payments.payment_order_id | payments_count: number of payment records for the order — derived from COUNT(payments.payment_id) | payments_amount_sum: sum of payment_amount for the order — derived from SUM(payments.payment_amount) | payments_fee_sum: sum of payment_fee for the order — derived from SUM(payments.payment_fee) | payment_status_any: a preserved payment_status value for the order (MIN used to pick a deterministic value) — derived from MIN(payments.payment_status)
params.metric: payments_count = COUNT(payments.payment_id)  -- cardinality metric: counts payment rows per payment_order_id | payments_amount_sum = SUM(payments.payment_amount)  -- additive monetary metric per payment_order_id | payments_fee_sum = SUM(payments.payment_fee)  -- additive monetary metric per payment_order_id | payment_status_any = MIN(payments.payment_status)  -- non-additive representative attribute; MIN used only to pick a deterministic value
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_enriched_with_store_channel_hub (JOIN) on payment_order_id = orders_enriched_with_store_channel_hub.order_id — safe because payments_by_order_agg has one row per payment_order_id, so attaching order attributes does not duplicate payments measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_daily_counts_and_amounts (AGG) on payment_order_id = orders_daily_counts_and_amounts.order_id (if that view is one-row-per-order) — safe only if the target is one-row-per-order; confirm the sibling view's grain before joining. | do NOT join payments_by_order_agg directly to deliveries_by_order_agg or drivers_with_delivery_stats if those sibling views are one-to-many relative to orders (e.g., multiple deliveries per order) without re-aggregation — joining a one-row-per-order payments view to a multi-row-per-order deliveries result will multiply payment measures. Instead, either: | - join to deliveries_by_order_agg on payment_order_id = deliveries_by_order_agg.delivery_order_id only if deliveries_by_order_agg is guaranteed one-row-per-order; or | - pre-aggregate or reduce the multi-row side to one row per order (e.g., SUM or COUNT on deliveries_by_order_agg grouped by order) before joining, so payments_amount_sum and payments_count remain correct. | do NOT join payments_by_order_agg to raw payments (payments table) or any other payment-level table without re-aggregation — that would reintroduce the original many rows and duplicate aggregates. | When composing across views: treat payments_amount_sum and payments_fee_sum as additive, order-level metrics safe to SUM across disjoint sets of orders; treat payments_count as a count-of-payments-per-order and only aggregate counts across orders (SUM over orders yields total payments). | Be cautious when joining to RANK or analytic views like store_rank_by_order_amount: ensure the rank view is at order grain (one row per order) before joining; otherwise compute a one-row-per-order projection of the rank (e.g., take MIN/MAX rank per order) to avoid duplicating payment aggregates.

views.description: Aggregated payment metrics rolled up to payment_order_id (the order-level payment connector). Returns sums and counts of payments and fees per payment_order_id. Useful to avoid row-multiplication when joining payments to orders and to support questions about total paid amount, total fees, or number of payment events per order. | Use for: Total paid amount, fees or number of payment attempts per order; Join-safe payment summary when combining with orders to compute net revenue per order

views.name: deliveries_by_order_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  delivery_order_id AS delivery_order_id,
  COUNT(delivery_id) AS deliveries_count,
  SUM(delivery_distance_meters) AS deliveries_distance_meters_sum,
  AVG(delivery_distance_meters) AS deliveries_distance_meters_avg,
  MIN(delivery_status) AS delivery_status_any
FROM deliveries
GROUP BY delivery_order_id

params.description: Per-order aggregates of deliveries: counts, distance sums/averages, and an example status value (lexicographically minimal).
params.when_to_use: Get delivery-level summary metrics for a specific order (e.g., number of deliveries, total distance, avg distance). | Join delivery summary metrics into order-level reporting, billing, or fulfillment dashboards. | Build further aggregations by order (e.g., daily order totals, store-level rollups) without re-scanning the deliveries table. | Filter/order/rank orders by deliveries_count or deliveries_distance_meters_sum.
params.output_schema: delivery_order_id: identifier for the order that deliveries are associated with — derived from deliveries.delivery_order_id (group key). | deliveries_count: number of delivery rows for that delivery_order_id — derived from COUNT(deliveries.delivery_id). | deliveries_distance_meters_sum: total of delivery_distance_meters for that delivery_order_id — derived from SUM(deliveries.delivery_distance_meters). | deliveries_distance_meters_avg: arithmetic average of delivery_distance_meters for that delivery_order_id — derived from AVG(deliveries.delivery_distance_meters). | delivery_status_any: a representative delivery_status for that order computed as MIN(deliveries.delivery_status) (lexicographically smallest status); not a deterministic existence/boolean indicator — derived from MIN(deliveries.delivery_status).
params.metric: deliveries_count = COUNT(deliveries.delivery_id)  -- cardinality metric (integer) counting delivery rows per delivery_order_id | deliveries_distance_meters_sum = SUM(deliveries.delivery_distance_meters)  -- additive metric (numeric) representing total distance per delivery_order_id | deliveries_distance_meters_avg = AVG(deliveries.delivery_distance_meters)  -- derived metric (numeric) equal to deliveries_distance_meters_sum / deliveries_count when deliveries_count > 0 | delivery_status_any = MIN(deliveries.delivery_status)  -- representative non-additive value chosen via MIN() over delivery_status; semantic: lexicographically smallest status among deliveries for the order
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_enriched_with_store_channel_hub (JOIN) on delivery_order_id = orders_enriched_with_store_channel_hub.order_id — safe because deliveries_by_order_agg is one-row-per-delivery_order_id, so its aggregated measures will not be duplicated when joined to the one-row-per-order view. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to payments_by_order_agg (AGG) on delivery_order_id = payments_by_order_agg.payment_order_id (or payments_by_order_agg.order_id) — safe when payments_by_order_agg is one-row-per-order aggregate; both are order-level aggregates so measures remain aligned and not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to store_rank_by_order_amount (RANK) on delivery_order_id = store_rank_by_order_amount.order_id — safe if store_rank_by_order_amount is one-row-per-order; preserves deliveries_by_order_agg measures. | unsafe-to-join guidance: do NOT join directly to the raw deliveries table or any one-to-many detail table (e.g., deliveries, order_items, payments raw table with multiple rows per order) without re-aggregation, because joining a one-row-per-order aggregate to a detail table that has multiple rows per order will multiply the aggregate row and incorrectly inflate additive metrics (deliveries_count, deliveries_distance_meters_sum). | unsafe-to-join guidance: do NOT join to drivers_with_delivery_stats (AGG) or other multi-order aggregates without verifying their grain. If drivers_with_delivery_stats is one-row-per-driver, joining it to deliveries_by_order_agg on a driver key (via orders_enriched_with_store_channel_hub or orders table) may be safe only when the join path preserves one-row-per-order; ensure join keys do not produce one-to-many multiplicity. | composition tips: when combining with other one-to-many dimensions, either (a) pre-aggregate the downstream detail to order-level before joining, or (b) join first and then re-aggregate, using SUM()/COUNT() over deliveries_by_order_agg measures where appropriate. For example, to roll deliveries up to store-day, join deliveries_by_order_agg to orders_enriched_with_store_channel_hub (one-row-per-order) then aggregate by store and date — this will not double-count because both inputs are order-grain. | explain avg consistency: deliveries_distance_meters_avg can be recomputed from deliveries_distance_meters_sum / NULLIF(deliveries_count,0) when composing; prefer recomputing averages from sum/count to avoid averaging averages across grouped subsets without weighting.

views.description: Aggregated delivery metrics rolled up to delivery_order_id. Provides count of deliveries, total and average delivery distance and a sample delivery_status. Useful to summarize delivery attempts or multi-part deliveries per order and to safely join to orders without multiplying rows. | Use for: Delivery counts and distances per order; Assessing orders with multiple delivery attempts or unusually long distances

views.name: orders_with_payment_and_delivery_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id AS order_id,
  o.store_id AS store_id,
  o.channel_id AS channel_id,
  o.payment_order_id AS payment_order_id,
  o.delivery_order_id AS delivery_order_id,
  o.order_status AS order_status,
  o.order_amount AS order_amount,
  p.payments_count AS payments_count,
  p.payments_amount_sum AS payments_amount_sum,
  p.payments_fee_sum AS payments_fee_sum,
  d.deliveries_count AS deliveries_count,
  d.deliveries_distance_meters_sum AS deliveries_distance_meters_sum,
  d.deliveries_distance_meters_avg AS deliveries_distance_meters_avg
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN payments_by_order_agg p ON o.payment_order_id = p.payment_order_id
LEFT JOIN deliveries_by_order_agg d ON o.delivery_order_id = d.delivery_order_id

params.description: Provides one-row-per-order summary combining order attributes with pre-aggregated payment and delivery metrics so you can query order-level amounts, counts, fees and delivery distances.
params.when_to_use: Get order-level reporting that needs payments and deliveries summarized per order (counts, sums, averages) without re-aggregating raw payment/delivery rows. | Filter or group by order attributes (store_id, channel_id, order_status) while using the attached payment/delivery metrics as order-level measures. | Compose higher-level aggregates (e.g., store- or daily-level totals) by aggregating this view at a higher grain (e.g., GROUP BY store_id) rather than joining raw payments/deliveries into orders directly.
params.output_schema: order_id: unique identifier of the order; derived from orders.order_id | store_id: identifier of the store that received the order; derived from orders.store_id | channel_id: sales channel for the order (e.g., web, app); derived from orders.channel_id | payment_order_id: foreign key on orders linking to the payments_by_order_agg payment_order_id (used to join payment aggregates); derived from orders.payment_order_id | delivery_order_id: foreign key on orders linking to the deliveries_by_order_agg delivery_order_id (used to join delivery aggregates); derived from orders.delivery_order_id | order_status: current status of the order; derived from orders.order_status | order_amount: monetary amount recorded on the order row; derived from orders.order_amount | payments_count: number of payment rows aggregated for this order; derived from payments_by_order_agg.payments_count | payments_amount_sum: sum of payment amounts for this order; derived from payments_by_order_agg.payments_amount_sum | payments_fee_sum: sum of payment fees for this order; derived from payments_by_order_agg.payments_fee_sum | deliveries_count: number of delivery rows aggregated for this order; derived from deliveries_by_order_agg.deliveries_count | deliveries_distance_meters_sum: sum of delivery distances (meters) for this order; derived from deliveries_by_order_agg.deliveries_distance_meters_sum | deliveries_distance_meters_avg: average delivery distance (meters) for this order; derived from deliveries_by_order_agg.deliveries_distance_meters_avg
params.grounded_columns: orders.order_id | orders.store_id | orders.channel_id | orders.payment_order_id | orders.delivery_order_id | orders.order_status | orders.order_amount | payments_by_order_agg.payment_order_id | payments_by_order_agg.payments_count | payments_by_order_agg.payments_amount_sum | payments_by_order_agg.payments_fee_sum | deliveries_by_order_agg.delivery_order_id | deliveries_by_order_agg.deliveries_count | deliveries_by_order_agg.deliveries_distance_meters_sum | deliveries_by_order_agg.deliveries_distance_meters_avg
params.metric: payments_count = payments_by_order_agg.payments_count (pre-aggregated count of payments per payment_order_id) | payments_amount_sum = payments_by_order_agg.payments_amount_sum (pre-aggregated sum of payment amounts per payment_order_id) | payments_fee_sum = payments_by_order_agg.payments_fee_sum (pre-aggregated sum of payment fees per payment_order_id) | deliveries_count = deliveries_by_order_agg.deliveries_count (pre-aggregated count of deliveries per delivery_order_id) | deliveries_distance_meters_sum = deliveries_by_order_agg.deliveries_distance_meters_sum (pre-aggregated sum of delivery distances per delivery_order_id) | deliveries_distance_meters_avg = deliveries_by_order_agg.deliveries_distance_meters_avg (pre-aggregated average of delivery distance per delivery_order_id)
params.composition: Join to orders_enriched_with_store_channel_hub on order_id — safe because that sibling view is one-row-per-order (same grain), so joining preserves this view's one-row-per-order cardinality and does not duplicate measures. | Join to store dimension or store_rank_by_order_amount on store_id — safe because store dimension / rank are one-row-per-store; joining will not duplicate order-level measures (each order maps to a single store row). | Join to drivers_with_delivery_stats only via a delivery-order-level key that is one-to-one with this view's delivery_order_id (if drivers_with_delivery_stats is aggregated per delivery_order_id). Otherwise, do NOT join directly to drivers_with_delivery_stats if it is one-to-many to delivery_order_id without re-aggregation, because that will duplicate deliveries_count and other delivery measures. | Do NOT join directly to payments_by_order_agg or deliveries_by_order_agg on keys that are not unique (unless you expect a 1:1) because those sources are already joined here; duplicating the same join is unnecessary but safe if identical — avoid joining to other payment/delivery raw tables that are one-to-many without re-aggregating, because that will multiply payments_count/payments_amount_sum/payments_fee_sum and deliveries_count/deliveries_distance_meters_sum. | When composing higher-level aggregates (e.g., totals by store_id or channel_id), aggregate the metrics in this view (SUM(payments_amount_sum), SUM(deliveries_distance_meters_sum), AVG delivered distances computed as SUM(deliveries_distance_meters_sum)/SUM(deliveries_count) when a true weighted average is needed) rather than joining raw child tables. This prevents double-counting because this view is one-row-per-order. | If you need to join to any table/view that is one-to-many with orders (for example, raw payments or raw deliveries), first aggregate that table to order_id (or the appropriate payment_order_id/delivery_order_id) to the same grain as this view before joining — otherwise the join will multiply this view's order-level metrics.

views.description: Order-level relation that joins orders to aggregated payment and delivery summaries (payments_by_order_agg, deliveries_by_order_agg). Use when analyzing orders together with payment totals and delivery aggregates while preventing multiplicative joins from raw payments/deliveries. | Use for: Compute net revenue per order (order_amount minus fees) using aggregated payment fees; Analyze correlation between delivery distance and payment outcomes at the order level

views.name: orders_daily_counts_and_amounts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_created_year AS order_created_year,
  order_created_month AS order_created_month,
  order_created_day AS order_created_day,
  COUNT(order_id) AS orders_count,
  SUM(order_amount) AS order_amount_sum,
  SUM(order_delivery_fee) AS order_delivery_fee_sum
FROM orders
GROUP BY
  order_created_year,
  order_created_month,
  order_created_day

params.description: Daily counts and sums of orders (count of orders, sum of order amounts, sum of delivery fees) at the date grain year-month-day derived from the orders table.
params.when_to_use: Get total number of orders and total order monetary amounts for a specific day or date range (by year/month/day). | Produce daily time series of order counts, order revenue, and delivery fee revenue. | Compose higher-level reports that need daily order-level aggregates as a reliable base (e.g., join to store or payment summaries at the order-day grain). | Use as an aggregation building block when computing rates or averages per day (e.g., average order amount = order_amount_sum / orders_count).
params.output_schema: order_created_year: calendar year of the order creation date — derived from orders.order_created_year (base column in orders table). | order_created_month: calendar month of the order creation date — derived from orders.order_created_month (base column in orders table). | order_created_day: calendar day-of-month of the order creation date — derived from orders.order_created_day (base column in orders table). | orders_count: count of distinct order rows for that year-month-day — derived as COUNT(order_id) over orders.order_id (aggregate). | order_amount_sum: total of order_amount for that year-month-day — derived as SUM(order_amount) over orders.order_amount (aggregate). | order_delivery_fee_sum: total of order_delivery_fee for that year-month-day — derived as SUM(order_delivery_fee) over orders.order_delivery_fee (aggregate).
params.grounded_columns: orders.order_created_year | orders.order_created_month | orders.order_created_day | orders.order_id | orders.order_amount | orders.order_delivery_fee
params.metric: orders_count = COUNT(orders.order_id)  -- count of order_id rows in orders for the group (order_created_year, order_created_month, order_created_day) | order_amount_sum = SUM(orders.order_amount)  -- sum of order_amount in orders for the group | order_delivery_fee_sum = SUM(orders.order_delivery_fee)  -- sum of order_delivery_fee in orders for the group
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension/lookups that are one-row-per-key without re-aggregation. For example, join to a store dimension or channel dimension on their key(s) if those dimensions are one-row-per-store or one-row-per-channel. This is safe because orders_daily_counts_and_amounts is already aggregated to one row per order_created_year, order_created_month, order_created_day and joining a 1:1 dimension (by the chosen key) will not duplicate measures. | safe join example: DO NOT join orders_daily_counts_and_amounts directly to orders_enriched_with_store_channel_hub on (order_created_year, order_created_month, order_created_day) unless the enriched view is also aggregated to the same date grain. orders_enriched_with_store_channel_hub is a JOIN (likely many rows per day) — joining it directly will multiply rows and duplicate measures. Instead, either (a) aggregate the enriched view to the same date grain first, or (b) join the enriched view to the base orders table prior to aggregation so the multiplication is handled before computing sums/counts. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many aggregates or detail tables (e.g., payments_by_order_agg, deliveries_by_order_agg, drivers_with_delivery_stats) without re-aggregation to the same date grain. These sibling AGG views typically produce multiple rows per day or per order; joining them directly will multiply orders_count/order_amount_sum/order_delivery_fee_sum unless you reduce the sibling to one row per (order_created_year, order_created_month, order_created_day) first. | When composing metrics: if you need to combine orders_daily_counts_and_amounts with payments_by_order_agg or deliveries_by_order_agg, either (a) aggregate the payment/delivery view to the same (year, month, day) keys and then join on those keys (safe because both sides are one-row-per-day), or (b) join at the order_id level before aggregation (i.e., start from orders or enriched orders and re-aggregate) so that sums/counts are computed correctly and not duplicated. | Planner rules summary: this view is one-row-per (order_created_year, order_created_month, order_created_day). Only join it without re-aggregation to other datasets that are guaranteed to be one-row-per the same date grain (or 1:1 by a deterministic key). Any join to a dataset that is 1:many into that grain requires re-aggregation of the many side (or re-computation from base tables) to avoid measure duplication.

views.description: Daily aggregated order counts and sums by order_created_year/month/day. Useful for time series of order volume and gross merchandise value (GMV) at the day grain. Keeps date parts as columns so consumers can filter or roll-up as needed. | Use for: Daily trends of order volume and revenue; Weekly/monthly rollups derived from daily aggregates

views.name: drivers_with_delivery_stats
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  deliveries.driver_id AS driver_id,
  COUNT(deliveries.delivery_id) AS deliveries_count,
  SUM(deliveries.delivery_distance_meters) AS delivery_distance_meters_sum,
  AVG(deliveries.delivery_distance_meters) AS delivery_distance_meters_avg,
  MIN(deliveries.delivery_status) AS delivery_status_any
FROM deliveries
GROUP BY deliveries.driver_id

params.description: Per-driver aggregates of deliveries: counts, total and average delivery distance, and a representative delivery_status value for each driver.
params.when_to_use: Report total number of deliveries per driver | Rank or filter drivers by total delivery distance or average delivery distance | Join driver-level delivery metrics into driver dimension tables or downstream reports without re-aggregating deliveries | Compose with other one-row-per-driver datasets (e.g., driver profiles) to enrich driver-level analytics
params.output_schema: driver_id: identifier for the driver; derived from deliveries.driver_id | deliveries_count: number of deliveries performed by the driver; derived from COUNT(deliveries.delivery_id) | delivery_distance_meters_sum: sum of delivery distances in meters for the driver; derived from SUM(deliveries.delivery_distance_meters) | delivery_distance_meters_avg: average delivery distance in meters for the driver; derived from AVG(deliveries.delivery_distance_meters) | delivery_status_any: a single (MIN) delivery_status value per driver (represents the minimum value according to the delivery_status ordering); derived from MIN(deliveries.delivery_status)
params.metric: deliveries_count = COUNT(deliveries.delivery_id) | delivery_distance_meters_sum = SUM(deliveries.delivery_distance_meters) | delivery_distance_meters_avg = AVG(deliveries.delivery_distance_meters) | delivery_status_any = MIN(deliveries.delivery_status)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver dimension or any one-row-per-driver view/table on driver_id — safe because this view has exactly one row per driver_id, so measures in this view will not be duplicated when joined (e.g., JOIN drivers ON drivers.driver_id = drivers_with_delivery_stats.driver_id). | do NOT join this view directly to orders, deliveries (raw) or any other one-to-many child table on driver_id without re-aggregation — doing so will multiply rows and thus overcount deliveries_count and sum/avg metrics. If you need order- or delivery-level detail combined with these metrics, either: (a) aggregate the child table to driver_id first and then join, or (b) join and then re-aggregate at the desired grain. | when composing with sibling AGG views (e.g., deliveries_by_order_agg or payments_by_order_agg), ensure joins are performed at compatible grains: this view is at grain driver_id, so join to other driver-level aggregates or to driver dimension; do NOT join directly to order-level aggregates without an explicit GROUP BY driver_id to avoid duplicating driver measures. | AVG composition note: delivery_distance_meters_avg is an internal AVG computed over deliveries for that driver. If you need an overall avg across a set of drivers, compute a weighted average using delivery_distance_meters_sum and deliveries_count (global_avg = SUM(delivery_distance_meters_sum) / SUM(deliveries_count)) rather than averaging delivery_distance_meters_avg to preserve correctness.

views.description: Aggregated delivery statistics per driver (driver_id). Returns counts, sum/avg distances and a sample delivery_status. Useful for driver performance, workload, and distance-related analysis. | Use for: Driver workload and average trip distances; Identifying drivers with many deliveries or outlier distance patterns

views.name: store_rank_by_order_amount
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.store_id AS store_id,
  s.store_name AS store_name,
  s.store_segment AS store_segment,
  COALESCE(SUM(o.order_amount), 0) AS store_order_amount_sum,
  COALESCE(COUNT(o.order_id), 0) AS store_orders_count,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(o.order_amount),0) DESC) AS store_rank
FROM stores s
LEFT JOIN orders o ON s.store_id = o.store_id
GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name, s.store_segment

params.description: Ranks stores by total order_amount and returns per-store sums, counts, and rank (one row per store).
params.when_to_use: Get the total order amount and order count per store and their rank by order amount. | Show top-N or bottom-N stores by order revenue for leaderboards or reports. | Compose into dashboards that compare store-level revenue and counts across store attributes (e.g., segment). | Use as a seeded aggregation when building further store-level metrics without re-scanning the orders table.
params.output_schema: store_id: unique identifier for the store (derived from stores.store_id). | store_name: store display name (derived from stores.store_name). | store_segment: categorical segment assigned to the store (derived from stores.store_segment). | store_order_amount_sum: total monetary amount of orders for the store — COALESCE(SUM(orders.order_amount), 0) aggregated per store (derived from orders.order_amount). | store_orders_count: total number of orders for the store — COALESCE(COUNT(orders.order_id), 0) aggregated per store (derived from orders.order_id). | store_rank: RANK() over stores ordered by store_order_amount_sum DESC — rank position of the store by total order amount (derived from the window over the SUM(orders.order_amount)).
params.metric: store_order_amount_sum = COALESCE(SUM(orders.order_amount), 0)  -- aggregated at grain stores.store_id | store_orders_count = COALESCE(COUNT(orders.order_id), 0)     -- aggregated at grain stores.store_id | store_rank = RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(orders.order_amount),0) DESC) -- window ranking over the aggregation per store
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to store/dimension tables that are one-row-per-store on stores.store_id — e.g., join to the base stores table or any store-level lookup on store_id is safe because this view is one row per store and such joins preserve the one-row-per-store cardinality, so store_order_amount_sum and store_orders_count are not duplicated. | do NOT join directly to a one-to-many table or view keyed by order_id (for example, orders_enriched_with_store_channel_hub or orders_with_payment_and_delivery_summary) without re-aggregation, because those joins would multiply rows per store and thereby inflate store_order_amount_sum and store_orders_count. If you need to combine with order-level or payment/delivery-level details, first aggregate those sources to store_id (e.g., SUM(payment_amount) BY store_id) and then join to this view on store_id. | do NOT join directly to deliveries_by_order_agg or payments_by_order_agg (order-level aggregates) on store_id unless those aggregations have been rolled up to store_id first; joining order-level aggregates to this store-level view will duplicate store rows and measures. | If composing additional store-level measures: compute the new measures at store_id (GROUP BY store_id) from the original detail tables (orders, payments, deliveries) or from sibling AGG views that are already aggregated to store_id, then join on store_id. This preserves correctness because this view's measures are defined at the store_id grain. | If you need to produce combined metrics that require per-order detail (e.g., average order size computed from raw orders), prefer to re-aggregate raw orders to store_id in the same query context rather than joining raw orders to this view.

views.description: Rank stores by total order_amount using a window function. Produces one row per store with aggregated measures and a rank (1 = highest total order_amount). Useful as a basis for top-N store queries by adding WHERE store_rank <= K downstream. | Use for: Top-N stores by GMV or order count; Tiering stores by revenue rank for segmentation
